newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss report finding more Mobutu riches.
newsitem.headline: Swiss report finding more Mobutu riches.

text.p: Switzerland said on Wednesday it had found more of toppled Zairean dictator Mobutu Sese Seko assets, a day after Swiss banks uncovered just $3.4 million of funds and the banking watchdog declared the matter closed.

Finance Ministry spokesman Hugo Schittenhelm said the government's own hunt among private persons, lawyers, firms and asset managers for Mobutu's wealth after Berne froze his assets in mid-May had begun to bear fruit, but he said these "more or less" corresponded to the banks' findings so far.

"We suppose that our findings, from the point of view of rough comparison, more or less correspond to the findings of banks. We are looking at these amounts very closely. In the next two or three weeks, it is not excluded that we could find other things.

The latest revelations came just a day after the Swiss Federal Banking Commission said six banks had uncovered 4.8 million Swiss francs ($3.4 million) in assets owned by Mobutu, his family or their associates.

This was the result of a formal government survey among 406 Swiss commercial banks in response to a demand from officials in the new Democratic Republic of Congo to report any Mobutu riches the Swiss might hold.
The sum was a fraction of the billions Kinshasa says Mobutu has stashed away here, and was disputed by a fierce government critic who predicted a long legal wrangle over Mobutu's riches.
An initial, informal survey of a dozen big banks in April had found nothing.

Federal Banking Commission (FBC) deputy director Daniel Zuberbuehler said the latest search found cash including two fat accounts in one bank, shares, bonds and a safe deposit box yet to be opened. He said the matter was considered closed.
Critics suspect the worst of Swiss banks, which were swept up in protracted scandals over the Swiss assets of such toppled dictators as the former Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos.

The banks are already struggling to clean up their image, tarnished by charges that they hoarded the wealth of Jews murdered by Hitler in World War Two and acted as a clearing house for looted Nazi gold.
